original_analysis.analysis_summary: The log set shows typical Windows system activity (registry writes, process accesses, DNS queries, WFP permits). However, a notable abnormal event is a privileged service call (EventID 4673) where the user sbeavers, via the Cortana SearchUI.exe process, attempted to acquire SeTcbPrivilege (Act as part of the operating system). This privilege is highly sensitive and its request from a regular user process is unusual and potentially indicative of a privilege‑escalation attempt. No encoded PowerShell commands were observed.
original_analysis.agent_reasoning: 1. Identified log types: Sysmon (process creation, registry changes, process access), Security (audit success/failure, privilege use), and Filtering Platform (network permits). 2. Normal baseline: frequent registry writes by SearchUI.exe, many svchost process accesses, DNS lookups, and WFP events are expected on a Windows host. 3. Abnormal patterns: EventID 4673 (privileged service call) with SeTcbPrivilege request from a user account; this is rare and high‑risk. 4. Used event_id_extractor_with_logs to validate EventIDs 13, 12, 4673, 5156. 5. Built a timeline around the SearchUI.exe process (pivot) to see surrounding activity – only normal registry writes and process accesses were present, confirming the 4673 event stands out. 6. No suspicious encoded commands were found, so decoder was not needed. 7. Classified the threat as high‑severity due to the attempted use of SeTcbPrivilege.

abnormal_events.event_description: Audit failure: A privileged service was called. User sbeavers (SID S-1-5-21-526538150-889687948-186688817-1106) attempted to invoke a privileged service via the process C:\Windows\SystemApps\Microsoft.Windows.Cortana_cw5n1h2txyewy\SearchUI.exe, requesting SeTcbPrivilege.
abnormal_events.why_abnormal: SeTcbPrivilege (Act as part of the operating system) is a highly sensitive privilege normally reserved for system services. Its request from a regular user process (Cortana) is atypical and may indicate an attempt to elevate privileges or misuse system components.
indicators: Audit failure indicating the request was denied (potentially blocked, but still suspicious)

tool_enrichment.timeline_context: Timeline built around SearchUI.exe (process ID 6196) shows surrounding events are normal registry writes (EventID 13, 12) and process accesses (EventID 10). The privileged service call stands out as the only high‑risk event in this window.

abnormal_events.event_description: Object access: svchost.exe (running as LOCAL SERVICE) accessed the registry key \REGISTRY\MACHINE\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\Lsa.
abnormal_events.why_abnormal: Frequent access to LSA (Local Security Authority) registry keys by svchost can be normal, but combined with the privileged service call it may indicate enumeration of security settings. Highlighted as a secondary indicator.
indicators: Process svchost.exe with LOCAL SERVICE context

tool_enrichment.timeline_context: These accesses occur repeatedly throughout the log window and are part of normal system behavior, but are noted due to proximity to the privileged service request.
